lessons.title: Introduction to React and JSX

questions.prompt: What does JSX let you write directly inside JavaScript?
A React component is just a JavaScript ____ that returns JSX.
A component can return multiple sibling elements without wrapping them in a single parent element or Fragment.

lessons.title: Props and Component Composition

questions.prompt: How does a parent component pass data down to a child component?
A component is allowed to modify (mutate) the props it receives.
The special prop that holds JSX nested between a component's opening and closing tags is called ____.

lessons.title: State and Event Handling

options: An array with the current value and a setter function
A Promise that resolves to the value
Nothing, it only has a side effect
questions.answer: An array with the current value and a setter function

questions.prompt: Calling the setter function returned by useState triggers a component ____.
You should mutate a state variable directly instead of calling its setter function.

lessons.title: Effects and Side Effects

questions.prompt: What does an empty dependency array `[]` mean for useEffect?
options: The effect runs once, when the component mounts
The effect runs on every render
The effect only runs on unmount
questions.answer: The effect runs once, when the component mounts

questions.prompt: To fetch data when a component first renders, you would use the ____ hook.
A function returned from inside useEffect is used to clean up before the next run or on unmount.

lessons.title: Rendering Lists and Building Forms

questions.prompt: In a controlled input, what determines the input's displayed value?
options: Nothing, it is uncontrolled by default

lessons.title: Final Project: Build a Task Board
lessons.content:
# Final Project: Build a Task Board

Time to combine components, props, state, effects, and forms into a real React app.

## Requirements

1. Render a list of tasks (`{ id, text, done }`) using `.map()` with a proper, stable `key`.
2. Let the user add a new task through a controlled form input.
3. Let the user toggle a task's done state and delete a task, updating state immutably (no direct mutation of the array or its objects).
4. Fetch an initial list of tasks from an API (or a mock async function) inside `useEffect` when the board first mounts.
5. Split the UI into at least three components, e.g. `TaskBoard`, `TaskForm`, and `TaskItem`, that communicate through props.

## Stretch goals

- Persist tasks to `localStorage` so they survive a page reload.
- Add filter buttons for All / Active / Completed.
- Show a loading state while the initial fetch is in flight.

Submit your repository link below when you are done, an instructor will review it before you can mark this lesson complete. Good luck! 🚀
